statement: Show that $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^{4}x\,dx=\frac{3\pi}{16}$, and state the value of the corresponding integral of $\cos^{4}x$.
solution: $\sin^{4}x=\left(\tfrac{1-\cos 2x}{2}\right)^{2}=\tfrac14(1-2\cos 2x+\cos^{2}2x) =\tfrac14\left(1-2\cos 2x+\tfrac{1+\cos 4x}{2}\right)=\tfrac38-\tfrac12\cos 2x+\tfrac18\cos 4x$. Integrating from $0$ to $\pi/2$: the cosine terms vanish, leaving $\tfrac38\cdot\tfrac{\pi}{2}=\tfrac{3\pi}{16}$. By symmetry $\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\cos^{4}x\,dx=\tfrac{3\pi}{16}$ as well.
hints: Expand and integrate term by term; cosine terms integrate to zero.
